visual.general_description: Grayscale frontal portable chest radiograph with a white ellipse and a black-outlined white arrow marking a large lucent cavity in the patient's right lung.
visual.detailed_description: Frontal (AP) grayscale chest radiograph of a tilted/rotated patient with multiple thin linear tube-like and wire-like densities crossing the chest and neck (plausibly lines, tubes or monitoring leads; none individually identified). Burned-in text at the upper left reads "06-Feb-2025" and "04:15", followed by a partly cropped line beginning "ORT AP SEMI-ER..." (read as a portable AP semi-erect label; the rest is cut off). A white "L" appears at the upper right of the image. A white ellipse on the image-left side (the patient's right, consistent with the L marker on the opposite side) encloses a large dark lucent space in the right upper-to-mid hemithorax with irregular, thick-appearing walls and internal strand-like or septation-like densities. A white arrow with black outline enters from the lower right of the image and points up and to the left at the lower-medial margin of the circled lucency. The remaining right lower lung and the left lung are largely lucent; the cardiac/mediastinal shadow lies at the image centre-right. No scale bar or ruler is present, so the approximately 12 cm size cannot be measured from the pixels.

visual.general_description: Axial chest CT in lung window with a black ellipse and green arrow marking a large air-filled cavity in the right anterior hemithorax, with two green dimension lines labelled 101.17 mm and 71.81 mm.
visual.detailed_description: Axial CT slice of the chest displayed in a lung window (lungs black, soft tissue and bone bright). A small "A" marker is at the top centre, consistent with anterior at the top; the heart lies to the image right, so the large cavity is on the image-left, i.e. the patient's right side. A black ellipse encloses a large, irregularly lobulated, uniformly black air-filled cavity lying directly beneath the anterior/lateral chest wall, with a bright soft-tissue rim that is thick along its lateral and posterior-medial edges (wall thickness cannot be separated from adjacent chest wall with certainty). No horizontal air-fluid interface is visible inside the cavity on this slice. Green crosshair measurement lines span the cavity: a roughly horizontal line and a roughly vertical line. The printed on-image labels are "101.17 mm" (top, joined by a dotted line to the right end of the horizontal line) and "71.81 mm" (lower left, next to the lower end of the vertical line); the line-to-label pairing is by proximity, and the line lengths are in a ratio close to the numbers (about 1.4). A thick green arrow with white outline enters from the lower right and points up and left at the lower margin of the cavity. The aerated lung below the cavity and the left lung (image right) show vessels; a small dark aerated region lies by the spine on the image right. Circular monitoring-lead-like rings are at the top right. The third dimension (12 cm) quoted in the caption is not shown on this slice, and contrast enhancement is not assessable in this lung window.

Further imaging with contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis showed multifocal airspace disease with a large cavitary lesion in the right upper lobe measuring 10 x 7 x 12 cm, with peripheral wall thickening and no internal fluid level.

limitations: Single axial slice (750 x 647 px); the lobar location (right upper lobe), multifocal airspace disease, contrast enhancement and the 12 cm dimension are caption/text claims not verifiable from this slice.
Printed values 101.17 mm and 71.81 mm are on-image overlay text (roughly 10.1 cm and 7.2 cm) consistent with the first two caption dimensions; the line-to-label assignment is inferred from proximity.
Wall thickening cannot be reliably separated from the adjacent chest wall on this window.
Single unlabelled panel; no panel letters present.
